title: Hypoglycaemic Infant with Massive Hepatomegaly
presentation: A 6-month-old infant presents with fasting hypoglycaemia, massive hepatomegaly (6 cm below costal margin), and a round 'doll-like' facies. Growth is delayed (weight and length <3rd centile). Parents report the child becomes jittery, sweaty, and lethargic between feeds.

actions.label: 📋 Feeding & family history
actions.clue: Parents report jitteriness and lethargy 3-4 hours after feeds. An older sibling died at 8 months with similar symptoms and 'an enlarged liver'. Baby is exclusively breastfed every 3 hours.
actions.finding: Family history of similar illness + symptomatic hypoglycaemia between feeds

actions.label: 🩺 General & growth assessment
actions.clue: Weight 5.2 kg (<3rd centile), length 60 cm (<3rd centile). Round face with full cheeks. Subcostal fat pads present. Muscle bulk reduced.
actions.finding: Growth failure, doll-like facies, truncal obesity

actions.label: 🩺 Abdominal examination
actions.clue: Liver firm, smooth, palpable 6 cm below right costal margin. Spleen not palpable. No ascites, no caput medusae.
actions.finding: Massive hepatomegaly without splenomegaly

actions.label: 🩺 Neurological examination
actions.clue: Lethargic but arousable. Cranial nerves intact. Mild hypotonia. Deep tendon reflexes 2+. No focal deficits, no seizures.
actions.finding: Lethargy with mild hypotonia, no focal signs

actions.label: 🧪 Fasting blood glucose
actions.clue: Fasting glucose: 38 mg/dL (normal 70-100). After 4-hour fast: 28 mg/dL with clinical deterioration.
actions.finding: Severe fasting hypoglycaemia

actions.label: 🧪 Serum lactate
actions.clue: Lactate: 6.5 mmol/L (normal <2.0). No improvement after glucose administration.
actions.finding: Marked lactic acidosis

actions.label: 🧪 Serum uric acid
actions.clue: Uric acid: 9.2 mg/dL (normal 2-5.5).
actions.finding: Hyperuricaemia

actions.label: 🧪 Lipid profile
actions.clue: Triglycerides: 850 mg/dL (normal <150). Total cholesterol: 280 mg/dL. HDL: low. Plasma appears lipaemic.
actions.finding: Severe hypertriglyceridaemia with hypercholesterolaemia

actions.label: 🧪 Urinalysis
actions.clue: Specific gravity 1.025. pH 5.5. Glucose: negative. Ketones: moderate positive. No protein, no blood.
actions.finding: Ketotic hypoglycaemia (appropriate ketone response)

actions.label: 🧪 Liver function tests
actions.clue: ALT 68 U/L, AST 82 U/L (mildly elevated). GGT 45 U/L. Bilirubin normal. Albumin 3.2 g/dL (slightly low). PT/APTT normal.
actions.finding: Mild transaminitis with slightly low albumin

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma ammonia
actions.clue: Ammonia: 28 μmol/L (normal 15-55).
actions.finding: Normal ammonia — rules out urea cycle disorders

actions.label: 🧪 Arterial blood gas
actions.clue: pH 7.31 (normal 7.35-7.45). pCO2 32 mmHg. HCO3 16 mmol/L. Base excess -6. Anion gap: 22.
actions.finding: High anion gap metabolic acidosis (lactic)

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma acylcarnitine profile
actions.clue: Normal acylcarnitine profile. No abnormal species detected. Free carnitine normal.
actions.finding: Normal — rules out fatty acid oxidation disorders (MCAD, VLCAD, carnitine deficiency)

actions.label: ⚡ Glucagon stimulation test (fasting)
actions.clue: After 4-hour fast: 1 mg IM glucagon → glucose rises from 28 to 32 mg/dL at 30 min (minimal response, expected rise >30 mg/dL). Postprandial glucagon also shows no response.
actions.finding: Glucagon unresponsiveness — indicates inability to mobilise hepatic glycogen

actions.label: 🔬 Abdominal ultrasound
actions.clue: Liver span 10 cm (markedly enlarged). Homogeneous echotexture. No focal lesions. No biliary dilation. Normal kidneys, spleen, pancreas.
actions.finding: Hepatomegaly with normal parenchyma

actions.label: ⚡ Liver biopsy with enzyme assay
actions.clue: Light microscopy: marked glycogen accumulation in hepatocytes. PAS-positive, diastase-labile. Electron microscopy: normal glycogen structure. Enzyme assay: glucose-6-phosphatase (G6Pase) activity <2% of normal. Glycogen content 6x normal.
actions.finding: Glucose-6-phosphatase (G6Pase) activity <2% of normal — severe deficiency

differentials.reason: G6Pase deficiency → fasting hypoglycaemia, lactate ↑, uric acid ↑, TG ↑↑. Glucagon unresponsive. Biopsy confirms.
Glucagon after meal raises glucose (G6Pase intact). Debranching enzyme deficiency. Also has myopathy.
Glucagon after meal raises glucose. Milder course. Liver phosphorylase deficiency. No hyperuricaemia.
Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia — ketones would be LOW/absent. Normal acylcarnitine profile.
No hepatomegaly (glycogen depleted). Postprandial hyperglycaemia, not fasting hypoglycaemia.

title: Newborn with Encephalopathy and Maple Syrup Odour
presentation: A 5-day-old full-term neonate presents with poor feeding, lethargy progressing to coma. Urine has a sweet, caramel-like odour. Pregnancy and delivery were uneventful. An older sibling died at 2 weeks of age with 'metabolic encephalopathy' of unknown cause.

actions.label: 📋 Perinatal & family history
actions.clue: Term delivery, normal BW 3.2 kg. Breastfeeding poorly since day 3. Sibling died at 2 weeks with lethargy and seizures, no diagnosis. Consanguinity: parents are first cousins.
actions.finding: Consanguinity + sibling death from encephalopathy → strong suspicion of autosomal recessive metabolic disorder

actions.label: 🩺 Neurological examination
actions.clue: Comatose, no response to pain. Pupils sluggishly reactive. Intermittent opisthotonus. Hypertonia with brisk reflexes. Bilateral Babinski sign. Moro reflex absent.
actions.finding: Severe encephalopathy with signs of brainstem involvement

actions.label: 🩺 Note body fluid odour
actions.clue: Urine and cerumen have a distinctive sweet, caramel-like odour reminiscent of maple syrup. Also detectable on the baby's breath.
actions.finding: Distinctive sweet, caramel-like odour (reminiscent of maple syrup)

actions.label: 🧪 Blood glucose
actions.clue: Glucose: 82 mg/dL (normal).
actions.finding: Normoglycaemia — rules out hypoglycaemic encephalopathy

actions.label: 🧪 Serum electrolytes + anion gap
actions.clue: Na 138, K 4.8, Cl 100, HCO3 18. Anion gap: 20 (elevated). pH 7.28. pCO2 35. BE -6.
actions.finding: High anion gap metabolic acidosis

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma ammonia
actions.clue: Ammonia: 35 μmol/L (normal 15-55).
actions.finding: Normal ammonia — rules out urea cycle disorders

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma amino acid profile
actions.clue: Leucine: 2150 μmol/L (normal 50-150). Isoleucine: 980 μmol/L (normal 20-80). Valine: 1450 μmol/L (normal 100-300). Alloisoleucine: PRESENT.
actions.finding: Markedly elevated branched-chain amino acids + alloisoleucine present

actions.label: 🧪 Urine organic acids
actions.clue: Massive elevation of branched-chain ketoacids: α-ketoisocaproate, α-keto-β-methylvalerate, α-ketoisovalerate. No methylmalonic acid. No propionic acid.
actions.finding: BCKA elevation with no methylmalonic/propionic acid — rules out MMA/PA

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma glycine
actions.clue: Glycine: 220 μmol/L (normal 150-350).
actions.finding: Normal glycine — rules out nonketotic hyperglycinaemia

actions.label: 🧪 Acylcarnitine profile (dried blood spot)
actions.clue: Normal acylcarnitine profile. No abnormal species.
actions.finding: Normal — rules out fatty acid oxidation and organic acidaemias

actions.label: 🧪 CSF analysis
actions.clue: Opening pressure normal. Cells: 2 WBC. Protein 45 mg/dL. Glucose 65 mg/dL (serum 82). CSF amino acids show markedly elevated BCAA. No organisms.
actions.finding: CSF BCAA elevation mirrors plasma — no meningitis

actions.label: 🔬 Brain MRI
actions.clue: Diffuse cerebral oedema with restricted diffusion in deep white matter, basal ganglia, and brainstem. 'Mickey Mouse' sign on DWI (symmetrical involvement of cerebellar peduncles, cerebral peduncles, and globus pallidus).
actions.finding: Characteristic MSUD neuroimaging — 'Mickey Mouse' sign

actions.label: ⚡ Genetic analysis (BCKDHA/B/C/D)
actions.clue: Homozygous missense mutation in BCKDHA gene (E1α subunit). Parents heterozygous. No parental phenotypes.
actions.finding: Homozygous BCKDHA (E1α) mutation — branched-chain α-ketoacid dehydrogenase defect

actions.label: ⚡ Fibroblast BCKDH enzyme assay
actions.clue: BCKDH complex activity: 4% of normal in cultured skin fibroblasts. Activity undetectable in leucocytes.
actions.finding: BCKDH complex activity 4% of normal — severe deficiency

differentials.reason: Pathognomonic alloisoleucine + BCAA elevation. BCKA in urine. Maple syrup odour. Autosomal recessive.
Methylmalonic acid NOT elevated. Different organic acid profile. No alloisoleucine.
Propionic acid NOT elevated. Odd-chain FAs normal. No alloisoleucine.
Isovaleryl metabolites absent. 'Sweaty feet' odour, not maple syrup.
Ammonia is NORMAL. UCDs present with hyperammonaemia, not BCAA elevation.
Glycine normal. No ketosis in NKH.

title: Dark Urine, Photosensitivity, and Abdominal Pain
presentation: A 35-year-old woman presents with severe colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, and constipation for 3 days. She reports dark reddish-brown urine and photosensitive bullous lesions on sun-exposed areas (dorsum of hands, forearms). No fever, no jaundice. Similar but milder episodes occurred in the past.

actions.label: 📋 Present & past history
actions.clue: Recurrent episodes since age 25, often triggered by fasting, alcohol, or oral contraceptive pills. Family history: mother had 'stomach attacks' and skin blisters. No gallstones, no hepatitis risk factors.
actions.finding: Recurrent acute attacks + family history + known triggers (fasting, OCPs, alcohol)

actions.label: 🩺 Skin examination
actions.clue: Dorsum of hands and forearms: vesicles, bullae, erosions, and milia in various stages of healing. Skin fragility. Hypertrichosis on temples. No jaundice, no pallor.
actions.finding: Photosensitive bullous lesions with skin fragility and hypertrichosis

actions.label: 🩺 Abdominal examination
actions.clue: Abdomen mildly distended, tympanitic. Bowel sounds absent. Mild diffuse tenderness, no guarding or rebound. Liver span 10 cm (normal). Spleen not palpable.
actions.finding: Ileus with mild abdominal tenderness, no organomegaly

actions.label: 🩺 Vital signs + CVS exam
actions.clue: BP 165/98 mmHg, HR 112 bpm, RR 20, Temp 37.1°C. Tachycardia, hypertension. No murmurs. Peripheral pulses intact.
actions.finding: Hypertension and tachycardia (autonomic dysfunction)

actions.label: 🧪 Urinalysis + Wood's lamp
actions.clue: Urine: dark reddish-brown. Dipstick: positive for porphobilinogen (PBG) and δ-aminolevulinic acid (ALA). Under Wood's lamp: urine shows pink-red fluorescence. Bilirubin negative. Urobilinogen normal.
actions.finding: PBG and ALA positive with pink fluorescence

actions.label: 🧪 Urine porphyrin fractionation
actions.clue: PBG: 45 mg/L (normal <2). ALA: 30 mg/L (normal <5). Uroporphyrin: moderately elevated. Coproporphyrin: normal.
actions.finding: Markedly elevated PBG and ALA with moderate uroporphyrin

actions.label: 🧪 Liver function + bilirubin
actions.clue: Total bilirubin 0.6 mg/dL. ALT 28, AST 32, ALP 85, GGT 22. Albumin 4.0. PT/APTT normal.
actions.finding: Normal LFTs — rules out hepatobiliary disease as cause

actions.label: 🧪 Serum amylase + lipase
actions.clue: Amylase 45 U/L (normal <100). Lipase 22 U/L (normal <60).
actions.finding: Normal pancreatic enzymes — rules out pancreatitis

actions.label: 🧪 Renal function + electrolytes
actions.clue: Creatinine 0.7 mg/dL. BUN 12 mg/dL. Na 138, K 3.8, Cl 98, HCO3 24. Normal.
actions.finding: Normal renal function — no acute kidney injury

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma porphyrin fluorescence scan
actions.clue: Plasma fluorescence peak at 615-620 nm (characteristic of PBG deaminase deficiency). No peak at 626 nm (rules out variegate porphyria).
actions.finding: Plasma fluorescence scan distinguishes AIP from VP

actions.label: 🧪 Faecal porphyrin analysis
actions.clue: Faecal coproporphyrin: mildly elevated. Faecal protoporphyrin: normal. No coproporphyrin III/I isomer ratio elevation.
actions.finding: No marked faecal porphyrin elevation — rules out HCP and VP

actions.label: 🔬 Abdominal ultrasound
actions.clue: Normal liver, normal gallbladder (no stones), normal pancreas. Mild small bowel dilatation with fluid levels (ileus).
actions.finding: No gallstones, no biliary pathology — ileus secondary to porphyria

actions.label: ⚡ RBC PBG deaminase enzyme assay
actions.clue: Erythrocyte PBG deaminase (hydroxymethylbilane synthase) activity: 38% of normal. Family screening: patient's mother and one sibling also have ~40% activity.
actions.finding: Erythrocyte PBG deaminase (HMBS) activity 38% of normal — partial deficiency

actions.label: ⚡ HMBS gene sequencing
actions.clue: Heterozygous missense mutation in HMBS gene (exon 10, c.517C>T, p.Arg173Trp). Same mutation found in affected mother.
actions.finding: Heterozygous HMBS missense mutation (exon 10, c.517C>T), shared with affected mother

actions.label: 🧪 Blood lead level
actions.clue: Blood lead: 3 μg/dL (normal <10). No basophilic stippling on peripheral smear.
actions.finding: Normal lead level — rules out lead poisoning (which can mimic AIP)

differentials.reason: PBG deaminase deficiency → ↑↑ PBG/ALA. Acute neurovisceral attacks. Photosensitivity. AD inheritance. Plasma fluorescence peak 615-620 nm.
Faecal protoporphyrin NOT elevated. Plasma fluorescence peak at 626 nm is diagnostic of VP but absent here.
Faecal coproporphyrin NOT markedly elevated. No isomer III/I ratio abnormality.
PCT has only skin lesions, NO acute attacks, NO PBG/ALA elevation. Uroporphyrin decarboxylase deficiency.
Lead level normal. No basophilic stippling. Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase → ↑ ALA but NOT PBG.
Normal amylase/lipase. Normal gallbladder on ultrasound. Normal LFTs.

title: Newborn with Musty Odour and Intellectual Regression
presentation: A 6-week-old boy is brought for routine follow-up. His mother reports a strange musty, mousy odour. Newborn screening was not performed at their rural clinic. He is fair-skinned with blue eyes despite both parents being dark. Early developmental milestones appear delayed.

actions.label: 📋 Birth & Feeding History
actions.clue: Born at term, normal delivery. Exclusively breastfed. No family history of metabolic disease. No newborn screen performed.
actions.finding: No newborn screen performed

actions.label: 🩺 Skin & Hair Examination
actions.clue: Skin is fairer than expected for ethnicity. Hair has a lighter hue than parents. Eczematous rash on trunk.
actions.finding: Hypopigmentation relative to parents — tyrosine/melanin pathway affected

actions.label: 🩺 Neurological Examination
actions.clue: Reduced social smiling. Mild hypotonia. Head circumference normal. No focal deficits.
actions.finding: Mild developmental delay, hypotonia

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Culture + CRP + FBC
actions.clue: Blood culture: no growth. CRP: 2 mg/L (normal). WBC: 8.2 ×10⁹/L, normal differential. No evidence of infection.
actions.finding: Sepsis excluded — not the cause of lethargy

actions.label: 🧪 TSH + Free T4
actions.clue: TSH: 2.1 mU/L (normal). Free T4: 14 pmol/L (normal). Congenital hypothyroidism excluded.
actions.finding: Thyroid function normal — hypothyroidism excluded

actions.label: 🩺 Urine Odour Assessment
actions.clue: Urine has a distinctly musty, mousy odour — phenylacetic acid. Diaper smells strongly.
actions.finding: Musty/mousy urine odour — phenylacetic acid accumulation

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Reducing Substances
actions.clue: Clinitest negative. No reducing substances in urine. Galactosemia and hereditary fructose intolerance excluded.
actions.finding: No reducing substances — galactosemia/HFI excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Ammonia
actions.clue: Ammonia: 42 μmol/L (normal). Urea cycle defect excluded — no hyperammonaemia.
actions.finding: Normal ammonia — urea cycle defect excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Amino Acids
actions.clue: Phenylalanine: 1,840 μmol/L (normal <120). Tyrosine: low. Branched-chain amino acids normal. All other amino acids normal.
actions.finding: Isolated markedly elevated phenylalanine — PKU

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Ferric Chloride Test
actions.clue: Urine turns blue-green — phenylpyruvic acid present. (Reaction also seen in MSUD — not specific alone.)
actions.finding: Positive ferric chloride — phenylpyruvic acid present

actions.label: 🧪 Branched-Chain Amino Acids (Urine)
actions.clue: Leucine, isoleucine, valine: all normal in urine. MSUD excluded — no branched-chain aminoaciduria.
actions.finding: Normal BCAA — MSUD excluded

actions.label: ⚡ Urine Pterins + DHPR Activity
actions.clue: Biopterin profile normal. DHPR activity normal. No evidence of BH4 deficiency.
actions.finding: Normal biopterin profile and DHPR activity — BH4 pathway intact

differentials.reason: Phenylalanine >1800 μmol/L, musty odour, hypopigmentation, normal BH4 pathway, no newborn screen
Urine pterins and DHPR activity normal — BH4 synthesis and recycling intact
No maple syrup odour, branched-chain amino acids normal on plasma and urine profile
TSH and free T4 normal — hypothyroidism excluded early
Blood culture negative, CRP normal, WBC normal — no infective cause

title: Male Neonate with Hyperammonaemia and Orotic Aciduria
presentation: A 3-day-old boy becomes lethargic and feeds poorly. By day 4 he is unarousable and requires ventilatory support. Plasma ammonia is 950 μmol/L. His mother recalls episodes of headache and vomiting after high-protein meals but was never investigated.

actions.label: 📋 Family & Maternal History
actions.clue: Mother has episodic headaches, vomiting, protein aversion — never diagnosed. A maternal uncle died in infancy with 'brain swelling'. X-linked pattern suspected.
actions.finding: Maternal carrier history — X-linked inheritance

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Culture + CRP + Lumbar Puncture
actions.clue: Blood culture: no growth at 48h. CRP: 4 mg/L. CSF: clear, no organisms, normal glucose and protein. Sepsis and meningitis excluded.
actions.finding: No infection — encephalopathy is metabolic

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Glucose
actions.clue: Glucose: 4.2 mmol/L (normal). Hypoglycaemia excluded as cause of encephalopathy.
actions.finding: Normal glucose — hypoglycaemic encephalopathy excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Ammonia
actions.clue: Ammonia: 950 μmol/L (normal <80 neonates). Critically elevated — urea cycle defect or organic acidaemia.
actions.finding: Severe hyperammonaemia — metabolic emergency

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Gas + Anion Gap
actions.clue: pH 7.48, bicarbonate 28 (respiratory alkalosis). Anion gap: 12 (normal). No acidosis — organic acidaemia less likely.
actions.finding: Respiratory alkalosis, normal anion gap — against organic acidaemia

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Amino Acids
actions.clue: Citrulline: 5 μmol/L (very low). Glutamine markedly elevated. Arginine low. No argininosuccinate detected.
actions.finding: Very low citrulline — block at or before OTC step

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Organic Acids
actions.clue: No elevated methylmalonic, propionic, or isovaleric acid. Organic acidaemia excluded as cause of hyperammonaemia.
actions.finding: Normal organic acids — organic acidaemia excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Orotic Acid
actions.clue: Orotic acid: massively elevated. Carbamoyl phosphate overflows into pyrimidine synthesis pathway — this distinguishes OTC from CPS-I.
actions.finding: Elevated orotic acid — OTC deficiency, not CPS-I

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Acylcarnitine Profile
actions.clue: Acylcarnitine profile normal. No fatty acid oxidation defect. Propionic or methylmalonic acidaemia excluded.
actions.finding: Normal acylcarnitines — FAO defect excluded

actions.label: ⚡ OTC Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: Hemizygous pathogenic variant in OTC gene confirmed. Mother is heterozygous carrier. X-linked recessive confirmed.
actions.finding: Hemizygous pathogenic variant in an X-linked urea cycle gene; mother heterozygous carrier

differentials.reason: Hyperammonaemia, very low citrulline, massively elevated orotic acid, X-linked family history, OTC mutation confirmed
CPS-I also gives low citrulline but orotic acid is NORMAL — carbamoyl phosphate does not overflow into pyrimidine pathway
Citrullinemia shows markedly ELEVATED citrulline — here citrulline is very low
Culture negative, CRP normal, CSF clear — encephalopathy is purely metabolic
Organic acidaemias cause metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap — pH and anion gap normal here, organic acids normal

title: Tall Teenager with Stroke and Downward Lens Dislocation
presentation: A 16-year-old boy is admitted after a DVT in his left leg. He is tall (193 cm) with long limbs and fingers. His ophthalmologist previously noted downward displacement of both lenses. His IQ is below average. No cardiac murmur.

actions.label: 📋 Family History & Diet
actions.clue: Father is tall. A maternal aunt had a stroke at 28. Normal diet, no restrictions. No joint hypermobility. No prior cardiac investigation.
actions.finding: Family history of premature thrombosis

actions.label: 🔬 Echocardiogram
actions.clue: No mitral valve prolapse. Aortic root diameter 28mm (normal). No aortic dilatation or dissection. Heart structurally normal.
actions.finding: Normal echo — aortic dilatation absent, Marfan less likely

actions.label: ⚡ FBN1 Gene Sequencing (Marfan)
actions.clue: No pathogenic variant in FBN1 gene. Marfan syndrome genetically excluded.
actions.finding: FBN1 normal — Marfan syndrome excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Thrombophilia Screen (Factor V Leiden, Protein C/S, Antithrombin)
actions.clue: Factor V Leiden: negative. Protein C, S, antithrombin: normal. Antiphospholipid antibodies: negative. No inherited thrombophilia found.
actions.finding: Standard thrombophilia screen negative — does not explain DVT

actions.label: 🩺 Slit-Lamp Examination
actions.clue: Bilateral ectopia lentis — lenses displaced DOWNWARD and nasally. Marfan causes upward dislocation. This direction is characteristic of homocystinuria.
actions.finding: Downward lens dislocation — homocystinuria, not Marfan

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Sodium Nitroprusside Test
actions.clue: Urine turns cherry-red — positive for disulfide compounds including homocysteine. Rapid bedside screen.
actions.finding: Positive nitroprusside — homocystinuria

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Amino Acids + Total Homocysteine
actions.clue: Methionine: markedly elevated. Total homocysteine: 280 μmol/L (normal <15). Cystine: low.
actions.finding: Elevated methionine and homocysteine with low cystine

actions.label: 🧪 Pyridoxine Trial (B6 100mg/day × 4 weeks)
actions.clue: Plasma homocysteine falls 60% on high-dose B6 — B6-responsive pattern. B6 (PLP) is cofactor for cystathionine β-synthase.
actions.finding: Homocysteine falls 60% on high-dose B6 — B6-responsive pattern

actions.label: 🧪 MTHFR Gene Mutation Screen
actions.clue: MTHFR C677T: heterozygous (mild effect). However methionine is markedly elevated here — MTHFR deficiency causes LOW methionine. This variant is not causative.
actions.finding: MTHFR variant not causative — methionine elevated, not low

actions.label: ⚡ CBS Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: Compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in CBS gene confirmed. Autosomal recessive.
actions.finding: Compound heterozygous CBS gene variants — autosomal recessive

differentials.reason: Downward ectopia lentis, DVT, homocysteine 280, elevated methionine, positive nitroprusside, B6-responsive, CBS mutation
Marfan: UPWARD lens dislocation, aortic dilatation, normal homocysteine, FBN1 mutation — all absent here
Standard thrombophilia screen entirely negative — does not explain lens dislocation or elevated homocysteine
MTHFR deficiency causes LOW methionine and elevated homocysteine — here methionine is markedly elevated, pointing to CBS deficiency
Cannot explain lens dislocation or marfanoid habitus — homocysteine is the unifying metabolite

title: Infant Found Unresponsive After Overnight Fast
presentation: A 5-month-old girl is found unresponsive in her cot after sleeping 10 hours. She was well the previous evening. Blood glucose is 1.2 mmol/L. No ketones in blood or urine. She is resuscitated with IV glucose. Her older sibling died of SIDS at 4 months.

actions.label: 📋 Feeding & Family History
actions.clue: Exclusively formula-fed. Sibling died of SIDS at 4 months — no metabolic workup done. Parents non-consanguineous, Northern European.
actions.finding: SIDS sibling — autosomal recessive FAO defect suspected

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Glucose + Ketones
actions.clue: Glucose: 1.2 mmol/L. Blood ketones: 0.1 mmol/L (expected >3.0 in fasting state). Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia — cannot oxidise fat.
actions.finding: Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia — fatty acid oxidation defect

actions.label: 🧪 Insulin + C-Peptide (during hypoglycaemia)
actions.clue: Insulin: 1.2 mU/L (appropriately suppressed). C-peptide: suppressed. Hyperinsulinism excluded — insulin is not driving the hypoglycaemia.
actions.finding: Insulin suppressed — hyperinsulinism excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Cortisol + Growth Hormone (stress sample)
actions.clue: Cortisol: 680 nmol/L (appropriately elevated). GH: 22 mU/L (elevated). Counter-regulatory response intact — not adrenal or pituitary cause.
actions.finding: Normal counter-regulatory hormones — endocrine cause excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Liver Function Tests + CK
actions.clue: ALT 85 U/L (mildly elevated). CK: 420 U/L (mildly elevated). Consistent with metabolic myopathy and hepatic involvement — nonspecific.
actions.finding: Mildly elevated ALT and CK — nonspecific metabolic stress

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Acylcarnitine Profile
actions.clue: C8 (octanoylcarnitine): markedly elevated. C6 and C10 also elevated. C8:C10 ratio >2. This pattern is characteristic of a fatty acid oxidation defect.
actions.finding: Elevated C8 acylcarnitine — MCAD deficiency

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Organic Acids
actions.clue: Elevated medium-chain dicarboxylic acids: suberic, sebacic, adipic acids. Hexanoylglycine present. Consistent with MCAD deficiency.
actions.finding: Medium-chain dicarboxylic aciduria — MCAD

actions.label: 🧪 Lactate + Glucagon Stimulation Test
actions.clue: Lactate normal (1.1 mmol/L). Glucagon response: glucose rises 2 mmol/L (adequate). GSD type I and III less likely — glycogen stores mobilisable.
actions.finding: Normal lactate, adequate glucagon response — GSD excluded

actions.label: ⚡ ACADM Gene Analysis
actions.clue: Homozygous c.985A>G (K329E) — most common mutation in Northern Europeans.
actions.finding: ACADM c.985A>G (K329E) homozygous — common acyl-CoA dehydrogenase variant

differentials.reason: Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, C8 acylcarnitine elevated, SIDS sibling, dicarboxylic aciduria, K329E homozygous
Insulin appropriately suppressed during hypoglycaemia — hyperinsulinism requires elevated or non-suppressed insulin
GSD I: no hepatomegaly, lactate normal, glucagon response adequate, acylcarnitine profile normal in GSD
Primary carnitine deficiency: very low total carnitine, C8 not specifically elevated — acylcarnitine profile here is diagnostic for MCAD
Cortisol appropriately elevated at 680 nmol/L during stress — adrenal axis intact

title: Teenager with Liver Disease, Psychiatric Symptoms, and Tremor
presentation: A 16-year-old girl is referred for abnormal LFTs found during investigation of depression and irritability over 6 months. She has a postural tremor noticed by her teacher. ALT is 180 U/L. She was initially treated for anxiety disorder.

actions.label: 📋 Psychiatric & Neurological History
actions.clue: Behaviour change preceded liver symptoms. School performance declined over 1 year. Occasional dysphagia. No alcohol. Parents note drooling at times.
actions.finding: Neuropsychiatric onset — organic cause likely

actions.label: 🧪 Hepatitis A, B, C, E Serology
actions.clue: HBsAg: negative. Anti-HCV: negative. HAV IgM: negative. HEV IgM: negative. All viral hepatitis excluded.
actions.finding: Viral hepatitis excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Autoimmune Screen (ANA, ASMA, LKM-1, IgG)
actions.clue: ANA: 1:40 (weakly positive — nonspecific). ASMA: negative. Anti-LKM-1: negative. IgG: 14 g/L (normal). Autoimmune hepatitis unlikely.
actions.finding: Autoimmune hepatitis excluded — antibodies negative or weakly positive

actions.label: 🧪 GGT + CDT + Alcohol History
actions.clue: GGT mildly elevated (50 U/L). CDT (carbohydrate-deficient transferrin): negative. Urine ethanol: undetectable. Alcohol excluded.
actions.finding: Alcohol-related liver disease excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Thyroid Function Tests
actions.clue: TSH and free T4 normal. Hyperthyroidism excluded as cause of tremor and psychiatric symptoms.
actions.finding: Thyroid function normal — thyroid excluded

actions.label: 🩺 Slit-Lamp Examination
actions.clue: Kayser-Fleischer rings bilaterally — golden-brown copper deposits at periphery of cornea in Descemet membrane.
actions.finding: Kayser-Fleischer rings present bilaterally

actions.label: 🩺 Neurological Examination
actions.clue: Wing-beating tremor. Dysarthria. Mild cogwheel rigidity. No pyramidal signs. Basal ganglia involvement.
actions.finding: Wing-beating tremor, dysarthria — basal ganglia copper toxicity

actions.label: 🧪 Serum Ceruloplasmin
actions.clue: Ceruloplasmin: 0.04 g/L (normal 0.2–0.4). Markedly low — cannot incorporate copper. Note: ceruloplasmin can be low in malnutrition too — needs confirmation.
actions.finding: Very low ceruloplasmin — copper metabolism defect

actions.label: 🧪 Serum Total Copper
actions.clue: Serum total copper: 7 μmol/L (low-normal). Misleading — most serum copper is bound to ceruloplasmin. Free (non-caeruloplasmin) copper is what's elevated.
actions.finding: Total serum copper low-normal — misleading, does not exclude Wilson disease

actions.label: 🧪 24-Hour Urine Copper
actions.clue: 24h urine copper: 380 μg/day (normal <40). Markedly elevated — copper excreted in excess as free copper spills into urine.
actions.finding: Elevated 24h urine copper — excess free copper spill

actions.label: 🔬 Liver Biopsy + Hepatic Copper Quantification
actions.clue: Hepatic copper: 650 μg/g dry weight (normal <50). Micro/macrovesicular steatosis. No cirrhosis yet. Confirms massive hepatic copper deposition.
actions.finding: Hepatic copper 650 μg/g — massive copper accumulation

actions.label: ⚡ ATP7B Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: Compound heterozygous ATP7B mutations confirmed. Autosomal recessive inheritance.
actions.finding: Compound heterozygous ATP7B mutations — autosomal recessive

differentials.reason: KF rings, low ceruloplasmin, elevated 24h urine copper, hepatic copper 650 μg/g, ATP7B mutation, neuropsychiatric onset
ANA weakly positive (nonspecific), ASMA and LKM-1 negative, IgG normal — KF rings and copper studies confirm Wilson
Full viral hepatitis serology negative — viral cause excluded
CDT negative, urine ethanol undetectable, history denies alcohol use
Psychiatric symptoms are secondary to copper toxicity in basal ganglia — KF rings and copper studies confirm organic cause

title: Jaundiced Neonate with E. coli Sepsis and Cataracts
presentation: A 10-day-old girl is admitted with jaundice, poor feeding, vomiting, and fever. She has been formula-fed since birth. Blood culture grows E. coli. The liver is enlarged and firm. Urine dipstick is positive for reducing substances but negative for glucose.

actions.label: 📋 Feeding & Family History
actions.clue: Standard cow's milk formula (contains lactose) since birth. First child. Parents are cousins (consanguineous). No prior illness.
actions.finding: Lactose-containing formula + consanguinity — galactosaemia likely

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Culture + Sepsis Screen
actions.clue: E. coli bacteraemia confirmed. CRP: 180 mg/L. WBC: 22 ×10⁹/L. Sepsis is real — but is it the primary diagnosis or a complication?
actions.finding: E. coli sepsis confirmed — may be secondary to an underlying metabolic cause

actions.label: 🧪 Serum Bilirubin (Direct + Indirect)
actions.clue: Total bilirubin: 180 μmol/L. Direct (conjugated): 140 μmol/L. Predominantly conjugated — hepatocellular or biliary cause.
actions.finding: Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia — liver disease, not haemolysis

actions.label: 🔬 Abdominal Ultrasound (Biliary)
actions.clue: Gallbladder and bile ducts normal. No biliary dilatation. Common bile duct normal. Liver enlarged and echogenic. Biliary atresia less likely.
actions.finding: Normal biliary anatomy — biliary atresia less likely

actions.label: 🧪 TORCH Serology (CMV, Rubella, Toxoplasma, HSV)
actions.clue: All TORCH serology negative. Congenital infection excluded as cause of liver disease and cataracts.
actions.finding: TORCH negative — congenital infection excluded

actions.label: 🩺 Ophthalmological Examination
actions.clue: Oil-droplet cataracts bilaterally on fundoscopy — nuclear cataracts from galactitol accumulation in lens. Not seen in biliary atresia or sepsis alone.
actions.finding: Oil-droplet cataracts — galactose accumulation in lens

actions.label: 🧪 Urine Reducing Substances (Clinitest vs Glucose Oxidase)
actions.clue: Clinitest positive (reducing substance present). Glucose oxidase strip negative. Non-glucose reducing sugar — galactose or galactose-1-phosphate.
actions.finding: Non-glucose reducing substance — galactosuria

actions.label: 🧪 RBC GALT Enzyme Assay
actions.clue: Galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase (GALT) activity: <1% of normal. Severely deficient.
actions.finding: GALT activity <1% of normal — severely deficient

actions.label: 🧪 RBC Galactokinase Assay
actions.clue: Galactokinase activity: normal. Galactokinase deficiency causes only cataracts without liver disease — excluded here by normal activity.
actions.finding: Galactokinase normal — galactokinase deficiency excluded

actions.label: ⚡ GALT Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: Homozygous Q188R mutation in GALT — most common severe galactosaemia mutation.
actions.finding: Homozygous Q188R GALT variant — severe galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase deficiency

differentials.reason: Oil-droplet cataracts, galactosuria, absent GALT activity, E. coli sepsis as complication, Q188R mutation
E. coli sepsis here is a known complication of galactosaemia — cataracts and galactosuria cannot be explained by sepsis alone
Normal biliary anatomy on ultrasound, cataracts and galactosuria are absent in biliary atresia
Full TORCH serology negative — congenital infection excluded
Galactokinase deficiency: cataracts only, no liver disease, no sepsis risk — galactokinase enzyme activity normal here

title: Pancytopenia with Massive Splenomegaly in an Ashkenazi Adult
presentation: A 38-year-old Ashkenazi Jewish man presents with fatigue, easy bruising, and a massively enlarged spleen extending 12 cm below the costal margin. Full blood count shows pancytopenia. He has had mild bone pain for 2 years.

actions.label: 📋 Ethnic & Family History
actions.clue: Ashkenazi Jewish background. Father had splenomegaly. No lymphadenopathy. No fever, night sweats, or weight loss. No alcohol.
actions.finding: Ashkenazi ethnicity + family splenomegaly — Gaucher disease likely

actions.label: 🧪 Full Blood Count + Film
actions.clue: Hb 8.2 g/dL, WBC 2.4 ×10⁹/L, Platelets 68 ×10⁹/L. Film: no blasts, no abnormal lymphocytes, no tear-drop cells. Hypersplenism pattern.
actions.finding: Pancytopenia — hypersplenism, no malignant cells on film

actions.label: 🧪 LDH + Uric Acid + Beta-2 Microglobulin
actions.clue: LDH: 380 U/L (mildly elevated — nonspecific). Uric acid: 5.2 mg/dL (normal). Beta-2 microglobulin: 2.1 mg/L (borderline). Lymphoma not excluded yet.
actions.finding: Mildly elevated LDH — nonspecific, lymphoma not excluded by these alone

actions.label: 🔬 CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis
actions.clue: Massive splenomegaly confirmed. Liver enlarged. No lymphadenopathy in chest, abdomen, or pelvis. No focal lesions. No ascites. Lymphoma less likely without lymphadenopathy.
actions.finding: Splenomegaly + hepatomegaly, no lymphadenopathy — lymphoma less likely

actions.label: 🔬 Bone Marrow Biopsy + Trephine
actions.clue: Gaucher cells — large macrophages with crinkled tissue-paper cytoplasm (glucocerebroside-laden). No malignant cells, no fibrosis. Dry tap not encountered.
actions.finding: Gaucher cells on marrow

actions.label: 🧪 Flow Cytometry (Peripheral Blood)
actions.clue: No clonal B or T cell population. No CD5+/CD23+ CLL pattern. No hairy cells. Lymphoproliferative disorder excluded.
actions.finding: No clonal lymphocyte population — lymphoma/CLL/HCL excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Leukocyte β-Glucocerebrosidase Activity
actions.clue: Enzyme activity: 8% of normal in dried blood spot. Markedly deficient.
actions.finding: β-Glucocerebrosidase activity 8% of normal — markedly deficient

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Chitotriosidase + CCL18
actions.clue: Chitotriosidase: 4,800 nmol/h/mL (markedly elevated — normal <150). CCL18 elevated. Disease activity biomarkers for monitoring treatment response.
actions.finding: Markedly elevated chitotriosidase — Gaucher disease activity

actions.label: ⚡ GBA Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: N370S/N370S homozygous — most common Gaucher mutation in Ashkenazi Jews. Type 1 (non-neuronopathic) confirmed.
actions.finding: GBA N370S/N370S homozygous — common Ashkenazi Jewish variant

differentials.reason: Ashkenazi ethnicity, massive splenomegaly, Gaucher cells on marrow, deficient β-glucocerebrosidase, N370S mutation
No lymphadenopathy on CT, no clonal population on flow cytometry, no malignant cells on marrow biopsy
No CD5+/CD23+ clonal B cells on flow cytometry, WBC low not elevated
No tear-drop cells on film, no dry tap on biopsy, no leukoerythroblastic picture
Niemann-Pick shows foam cells not crinkled-paper cells, sphingomyelinase deficient not glucocerebrosidase

title: Infant with Cherry-Red Spot, Exaggerated Startle, No Organomegaly
presentation: A 5-month-old Ashkenazi Jewish infant is brought in for failure to reach milestones. Her mother notes an exaggerated startle to sounds. Fundoscopy reveals a cherry-red spot at the macula. The spleen and liver are not enlarged.

actions.label: 📋 Ethnic & Family History
actions.clue: Both parents Ashkenazi Jewish. A maternal cousin diagnosed with a lysosomal storage disorder. No prior screening. No consanguinity.
actions.finding: Ashkenazi ethnicity + family storage disorder — Tay-Sachs likely

actions.label: 🩺 Fundoscopy
actions.clue: Cherry-red spot at fovea bilaterally — pale surrounding retina from lipid-laden ganglion cells, fovea is spared and appears red.
actions.finding: Cherry-red spot — ganglion cell storage

actions.label: 🩺 Abdominal Examination
actions.clue: No hepatomegaly. No splenomegaly. Abdomen soft and flat. This is a critical negative finding — absence of organomegaly narrows the diagnosis.
actions.finding: No organomegaly — helps distinguish the sphingolipidoses

actions.label: 🩺 Neurological Examination
actions.clue: Hypotonia. Loss of head control. Hyperacusis — exaggerated blink/startle to hand clap. No seizures yet. Progressive neurodegeneration.
actions.finding: Progressive regression, hyperacusis

actions.label: 🔬 Brain MRI
actions.clue: Bilateral thalamic signal abnormality (T2 hypointensity). White matter changes developing. Consistent with lysosomal storage disorder — not specific to Tay-Sachs.
actions.finding: Thalamic signal change — lysosomal storage, nonspecific

actions.label: 🧪 Total Hexosaminidase Activity
actions.clue: Total hexosaminidase: normal. This is misleading — HexB compensates for absent HexA, so total activity appears normal. Must fractionate.
actions.finding: Total hexosaminidase normal — MISLEADING, must check HexA separately

actions.label: 🧪 Hexosaminidase A Activity (Fractionated)
actions.clue: HexA activity: <1% of normal. HexB activity: normal. Isolated HexA deficiency. (Sandhoff would show absent HexA AND HexB.)
actions.finding: Absent HexA with normal HexB — isolated HexA deficiency

actions.label: 🧪 Acid Sphingomyelinase Activity
actions.clue: Sphingomyelinase activity: normal. Niemann-Pick A excluded — sphingomyelinase is deficient in Niemann-Pick, not here.
actions.finding: Normal sphingomyelinase — Niemann-Pick excluded

actions.label: ⚡ HEXA Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: Homozygous 4-bp insertion in exon 11 of HEXA — classic Ashkenazi Jewish mutation.
actions.finding: Homozygous 4-bp insertion in exon 11 of HEXA — Ashkenazi Jewish variant

differentials.reason: Cherry-red spot, hyperacusis, NO organomegaly, absent HexA only, Ashkenazi ethnicity, HEXA mutation
Niemann-Pick always has hepatosplenomegaly — absent here. Sphingomyelinase normal, not deficient
Sandhoff: both HexA AND HexB absent. Here only HexA absent. Total hexosaminidase is normal — misleading if not fractionated
Gaucher does not cause cherry-red spot, and causes hepatosplenomegaly
Krabbe: galactocerebrosidase deficient, globoid cells, no cherry-red spot, very high CSF protein

title: Middle-Aged Man with Bronze Skin, Diabetes, and Arthritis
presentation: A 48-year-old man presents with fatigue, joint pain in his knuckles, and impotence. Examination reveals bronze-coloured skin and tender MCP joints. Random glucose is 14 mmol/L. His brother was recently diagnosed with liver cirrhosis.

actions.label: 📋 Family, Alcohol & Transfusion History
actions.clue: Non-drinker. Brother has cirrhosis of unknown cause. Father died of liver cancer at 52. Northern European ancestry. No blood transfusions, no IV drug use.
actions.finding: Family clustering of liver disease — hereditary condition, not lifestyle

actions.label: 🧪 Liver Function Tests
actions.clue: ALT 68 U/L (mildly elevated). AST 55 U/L. Bilirubin normal. ALP normal. GGT 80 U/L. Mild hepatocellular pattern — nonspecific.
actions.finding: Mild hepatocellular inflammation — nonspecific

actions.label: 🧪 GGT + CDT + Alcohol Markers
actions.clue: GGT mildly elevated (as above). CDT: negative. Urine ethanol: negative. Mean corpuscular volume: normal. Alcohol-related liver disease excluded.
actions.finding: Alcohol markers negative — alcoholic liver disease excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Hepatitis B + C Serology
actions.clue: HBsAg: negative. Anti-HBc: negative. Anti-HCV: negative. Viral hepatitis excluded as cause.
actions.finding: Viral hepatitis excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Iron Studies (Serum Iron, TIBC, Ferritin, Transferrin Saturation)
actions.clue: Ferritin: 4,200 ng/mL (normal <300). Transferrin saturation: 88% (normal <45%). Serum iron markedly elevated. Massive iron overload confirmed.
actions.finding: Ferritin 4200, transferrin saturation 88% — iron overload

actions.label: 🧪 Serum Ceruloplasmin + Urine Copper
actions.clue: Ceruloplasmin: 0.22 g/L (normal). 24h urine copper: 18 μg (normal). Wilson disease excluded — copper metabolism normal.
actions.finding: Normal copper studies — Wilson disease excluded

actions.label: 🔬 X-ray of Hands
actions.clue: Chondrocalcinosis of MCP joints (calcium pyrophosphate deposition). Hook-shaped osteophytes on 2nd and 3rd MCPs. Classic haemochromatosis arthropathy.
actions.finding: MCP chondrocalcinosis — classic haemochromatosis arthropathy

actions.label: 🔬 Liver MRI (T2* Sequence)
actions.clue: Marked hepatic iron deposition on T2* (low signal liver). No cirrhosis. No focal lesion. Cardiac T2* normal — no cardiac iron overload yet.
actions.finding: Hepatic iron overload on MRI

actions.label: ⚡ HFE Gene Analysis (C282Y/H63D)
actions.clue: Homozygous C282Y in HFE gene — most common genotype in Northern Europeans.
actions.finding: HFE C282Y homozygous — most common HFE genotype in Northern Europeans

differentials.reason: Bronze skin, diabetes, MCP arthropathy, ferritin 4200, transferrin saturation 88%, HFE C282Y homozygous, family history of liver disease
Non-drinker, CDT negative, urine ethanol negative, MCV normal — HFE mutation confirms hereditary cause
Ceruloplasmin and urine copper entirely normal — copper metabolism intact
Full viral hepatitis serology negative
No transfusion or IV drug use history; HFE mutation confirms primary genetic iron overload

title: Young Man with Haemolysis After Antimalarial Drug
presentation: A 24-year-old West African man starts primaquine for malaria prophylaxis. After 3 days he develops dark urine, pallor, and fatigue. Haemoglobin drops from 13.5 to 7.2 g/dL. Reticulocyte count 12%. No prior history of anaemia.

actions.label: 📋 Drug, Diet & Family History
actions.clue: Primaquine started 3 days ago. Previously tolerated quinine. Triggers in family: fava beans, dapsone, nitrofurantoin. Brother had similar episode with dapsone.
actions.finding: Oxidant drug-triggered haemolysis — G6PD deficiency likely

actions.label: 🧪 Direct & Indirect Coombs Test
actions.clue: Direct Coombs: negative. Indirect Coombs: negative. Autoimmune haemolytic anaemia excluded — haemolysis is non-immune.
actions.finding: Coombs negative — AIHA excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Blood Film + Reticulocyte Count
actions.clue: Heinz bodies on crystal violet stain — denatured Hb precipitates. Bite cells (degmacytes). Polychromasia. Reticulocytosis 12%. No sickle cells, no spherocytes.
actions.finding: Heinz bodies + bite cells — oxidative haemolysis

actions.label: 🧪 LDH + Haptoglobin + Indirect Bilirubin
actions.clue: LDH 980 U/L (elevated). Haptoglobin: undetectable. Indirect bilirubin elevated. Confirms intravascular haemolysis. Nonspecific — does not identify cause.
actions.finding: Intravascular haemolysis confirmed — nonspecific

actions.label: 🧪 Haemoglobin Electrophoresis
actions.clue: HbA: 97%, HbA2: 2.4%, HbS: 0%, HbC: 0%. Normal haemoglobin electrophoresis. Sickle cell disease and HbC disease excluded.
actions.finding: Normal Hb electrophoresis — haemoglobinopathy excluded

actions.label: 🧪 Flow Cytometry (CD55/CD59 for PNH)
actions.clue: CD55 and CD59 expression normal on RBCs and WBCs. Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria excluded.
actions.finding: PNH excluded — complement-mediated haemolysis not present

actions.label: 🧪 G6PD Enzyme Assay
actions.clue: G6PD activity: 5% of normal. Tested 2 weeks after episode (young RBCs have more G6PD — test during crisis underestimates deficiency). Severely deficient.
actions.finding: G6PD activity 5% of normal — tested 2 weeks after the episode

actions.label: 🧪 Pyruvate Kinase Assay
actions.clue: Pyruvate kinase activity: normal. PK deficiency excluded — PK deficiency causes chronic non-episodic haemolysis without Heinz bodies.
actions.finding: PK normal — pyruvate kinase deficiency excluded

actions.label: ⚡ G6PD Gene Analysis
actions.clue: G202A mutation (G6PD A- variant) — most common African variant. Hemizygous in this male — X-linked pattern.
actions.finding: G202A (G6PD A-) hemizygous — common African variant

differentials.reason: Oxidant drug trigger, Heinz bodies and bite cells, Coombs-negative, 5% G6PD activity, G6PD A- mutation, X-linked family pattern
Direct and indirect Coombs both negative — immune-mediated haemolysis excluded
No sickle cells on film, haemoglobin electrophoresis normal — HbS absent
PK deficiency causes chronic non-episodic haemolysis with echinocytes not bite cells — PK activity normal here
CD55 and CD59 expression normal on flow cytometry — complement-mediated haemolysis excluded

title: Boy with Self-Mutilation, Gout, and Choreoathetosis
presentation: A 3-year-old boy with intellectual disability repeatedly bites his fingers and lips, causing tissue loss. He has choreoathetotic movements. Serum uric acid is 11.8 mg/dL. His mother is neurologically normal. He was initially referred for cerebral palsy.

actions.label: 📋 Birth & Developmental History
actions.clue: Normal birth. Development normal until 6 months. Progressive neurological deterioration. Self-biting began age 2 — distressed by own behaviour. No family history in males.
actions.finding: Progressive regression with compulsive self-mutilation — not static CP

actions.label: 🔬 Brain MRI
actions.clue: Basal ganglia signal abnormality (caudate and putamen). Cortex preserved. No structural lesion, no periventricular leukomalacia. Basal ganglia dysfunction.
actions.finding: Basal ganglia changes — not typical CP (periventricular injury)

actions.label: 🧪 Plasma Amino Acids + Urine Organic Acids
actions.clue: Plasma amino acids: normal. Urine organic acids: normal. No aminoacidopathy, no organic acidaemia. Metabolic screen does not identify the defect here.
actions.finding: Amino acids and organic acids normal — standard metabolic screen unhelpful

actions.label: 🩺 Neurological Examination
actions.clue: Choreoathetosis, dystonia, hyperreflexia. Compulsive self-biting of lips and fingers — child appears distressed by own actions. Intellectual disability.
actions.finding: Compulsive self-mutilation + choreoathetosis — Lesch-Nyhan pattern

actions.label: 🩺 Joint & Skin Examination
actions.clue: Swollen tender first MTP joint. Tophi on ears. Gouty arthritis in a toddler — extraordinarily unusual. Points to massive urate overproduction.
actions.finding: Childhood gout + tophi — gross purine overproduction

actions.label: 🧪 Serum Uric Acid + 24h Urine Uric Acid
actions.clue: Serum urate: 11.8 mg/dL. 24h urine uric acid: 1,800 mg (normal <600 in children). Overproduction confirmed — not merely underexcretion.
actions.finding: Gross urate overproduction — not renal underexcretion

actions.label: 🧪 Renal Function + Urinalysis
actions.clue: Creatinine normal. eGFR normal. No haematuria. Uric acid crystals in urine. Renal failure as cause of hyperuricaemia excluded.
actions.finding: Normal renal function — hyperuricaemia is not from renal failure

actions.label: 🧪 RBC HGPRTase Enzyme Activity
actions.clue: HGPRTase (HPRT) activity: <1% of normal in RBC lysate. Complete deficiency. No purine salvage — de novo synthesis unchecked.
actions.finding: HGPRTase (HPRT) activity <1% of normal — complete deficiency

actions.label: ⚡ HPRT1 Gene Sequencing
actions.clue: Hemizygous pathogenic variant in HPRT1 gene. Mother confirmed carrier (heterozygous). X-linked recessive pattern.
actions.finding: Hemizygous HPRT1 gene variant; mother confirmed heterozygous carrier

differentials.reason: Pathognomonic self-mutilation, choreoathetosis, uric acid 11.8, childhood gout, absent HGPRTase, HPRT1 mutation, X-linked
CP is static — progressive regression, normal uric acid in CP, no self-mutilation as a feature, MRI shows basal ganglia not periventricular injury
PRPP superactivity causes hyperuricaemia but HGPRTase activity is normal and neurological features are absent
Plasma amino acids and urine organic acids entirely normal — standard metabolic screen unhelpful and negative
Renal function entirely normal — hyperuricaemia is from overproduction, not underexcretion

title: Woman with PKU Planning Pregnancy
presentation: A 26-year-old woman with known PKU becomes pregnant at 8 weeks. She had relaxed her phenylalanine-restricted diet 18 months before conception. Her pre-pregnancy phenylalanine levels were elevated at 900 μmol/L. She is now urgently concerned about her unborn child.

actions.label: 📋 Dietary Compliance & Conception History
actions.clue: Diet relaxed 18 months before conception — Phe up to 900 μmol/L during this period. Now 8 weeks pregnant. Critical window for organogenesis already partly elapsed.
actions.finding: Elevated maternal Phe during organogenesis — teratogenic window breached

actions.label: 🧪 Maternal Plasma Phenylalanine (Weekly)
actions.clue: Current Phe: 750 μmol/L. Target in pregnancy: 120–360 μmol/L. Dietary restriction and Phe-free formula urgently restarted.
actions.finding: Maternal Phe 750 — above safe pregnancy range

actions.label: 🧪 BH4 (Sapropterin) Challenge
actions.clue: No significant Phe reduction after BH4 loading. Mother has BH4-non-responsive PAH deficiency. Diet remains the only management option for her.
actions.finding: BH4-non-responsive — dietary restriction only

actions.label: 🧪 Fetal PAH Genotyping (CVS at 11 weeks)
actions.clue: Father: heterozygous PAH carrier. Fetus: heterozygous PAH carrier only. Fetus will NOT have PKU. However, fetal brain damage is from maternal Phe crossing placenta — not fetal enzyme deficiency.
actions.finding: Fetus is carrier only — fetal PKU excluded, but maternal Phe is still teratogenic

actions.label: 🔬 Nuchal Translucency + 12-week Ultrasound
actions.clue: NT: 1.8mm (normal). No structural anomaly detected at 12 weeks. Normal at this stage does not exclude later microcephaly or cardiac defect.
actions.finding: Normal 12-week scan — does not exclude later manifestations

actions.label: 🔬 Fetal Anomaly Scan (20 weeks)
actions.clue: Fetal head circumference on 3rd centile — early microcephaly developing. Cardiac four-chamber view: VSD detected. Features of maternal PKU embryopathy.
actions.finding: Microcephaly + VSD — maternal PKU embryopathy

actions.label: 🔬 Fetal Echocardiogram
actions.clue: Perimembranous VSD confirmed. No other cardiac defects.
actions.finding: VSD confirmed — structural cardiac defect

actions.label: ⚡ Fetal Brain MRI (30 weeks)
actions.clue: Reduced cerebral cortical development. White matter signal abnormality. Pachygyria pattern. Brain injury from first-trimester exposure — irreversible.
actions.finding: Fetal brain malformation — consistent with early teratogenic exposure

differentials.reason: Known maternal PKU, Phe 900 μmol/L in first trimester, fetal microcephaly, VSD, brain malformation on MRI — classic embryopathy
CVS confirms fetus is only a heterozygous carrier — fetal enzyme is intact. Damage is from maternal Phe crossing placenta
Maternal rubella serology negative — maternal PKU fully explains all cardiac and neurological findings
NT normal at 12 weeks, chromosomal microarray normal on CVS sample — trisomy excluded
VSD occurs in the context of elevated maternal Phe with microcephaly — not isolated, consistent with systemic teratogenic effect
